chapter: Louis Armstrong and leaving New Orleans
title: First hearing Louis Armstrong and Joe Oliver on Labor Day parade
summary: Ory heard a young trumpeter in the Labor Day parade and kept him in mind; Mutt Carey and Oliver played with Ory.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Hey-oh. Fair off and go, huh? When do you first remember seeing Louis Armstrong? On a parade on a Labor Day. He was an extra band.
The kid band. I was a kid band.
I was a kid band. I was a kid band. The Kidman, you know, from Holmes.
Oh, you mean he had a band of his own?
No, that was the Holmes band.
The Worthy. Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah. He and Kid René. He and Kid René were in the band? Yeah, they were both in there. Did your band play in the Labor Day Parade, too?
Yeah, my band was right in front of it. I heard a trumpet back there.
Was it, this is a little later, or about the same time as? Well. Oh, that was... A few years later? Around 1912, wasn't it? Papa Mudd was with me then. Papa Mudd was playing trumpet.
You heard this... No, it was Matthew playing trumpet. It wasn't Matthew.

You heard this trumpet behind you? Yeah. And, you know, a nice good solid tone, you know. And I turned around and we stopped for a break, you know. And we had quit playing and they were still playing. We stopped for a beer break, you know, a sandwich. And he was blowing and I stopped him. I said, come here, I'm telling you. I said, you're doing a good job. I said, thank you, Mr. Murray. I said, you're going to be all right someday, you keep it up. It's all right. So I kept him in mind all the time. I take mud after I met him after he dropped out and later...
Did you used to see him here and there? Who? Did you run into him?
Well, he got out right after that, you know. Yeah. He got out of the home. Yeah. And he used to run, little honky-tonk, go in there and play a little bit. You know, he loved it.
It wasn't right after that, honey.
Yeah. I mean, a while after that. Yeah, a while after that. I can't recall just how long. Well, I had mud after that. After that? Then I had olive. Uh-huh.
Until finally 1916 rolled around. Then he had Louis.
